subject: Science
title: Choose a rock for a job
objective_verbatim: Identify everyday uses of different rocks (links D&T / Construction).

success_criteria: I can name one rock use.
I can check one rock feature.
I can say why the feature helps.

retrieval.question: What two checks did we use on rocks?

worked_example.full: This slate sample is thin. Slate can make a roof tile. I match it to a roof.
worked_example.faded: This sample leaves a mark on the small board. I match it to ____.

worked_example.fade_next: Show an unlabelled safe sample and job cards; pupil tests and gives a reason.

cfu.question: What feature of the slate helped our roof example?
cfu.answer: It is thin and can be made into a roofing slate.

hinge.question: A new sample stays firm in a safe pressure test. Which possible job fits that clue?

options.text: A writing stick if it leaves a mark.
options.diagnosis: A mark was not observed in this test.

options.text: A path stone if it stays firm.
options.diagnosis: Uses the observed firmness for a possible job, subject to more checks.

options.text: A sponge if it soaks up water.
options.diagnosis: Water uptake was not observed in this test.

options.text: A window if it lets through light.
options.diagnosis: Light transmission was not observed in this test.

hinge.decision_rule: About 3 in 4 or more right → move on; otherwise re-model This slate sample is thin. Slate can make a roof tile. I match it to a roof. Ask the parallel hinge. No scores or answers saved.
hinge.parallel_hinge: A different sample D splits into broad thin sheets. Which job could be checked next: a roof covering or a soft marking stick? A roof covering, after further checks.

misconceptions.misconception: A named rock is good for every job.
misconceptions.spot: Matches one sample to all jobs.
misconceptions.correction: Check a feature needed for each job.

misconceptions.misconception: Colour alone tells whether a rock will make a mark.
misconceptions.correction: Try the teacher-approved marking test on a small board.

we_do.support: Point to one job card. Feel one safe sample.
we_do.stretch: Could one rock be good for one job but poor for another?

tiers.F: Match one sample to one job.
tiers.M: Choose a rock and say what feature helps.
tiers.H: Why could a soft rock fail on a busy path?

stems.M: This ____ can do the job as it is ____.

tiers.early_finisher: Choose a sample for a roof and a mark. Test each reason.

facts.claim: Different materials, including rock, can suit different everyday uses because of their physical properties.
Slate and stone have been used as roof coverings.
A sample that makes a safe mark can be matched to marking a board on direct observation; not every chalk-like rock behaves alike.
Hardness, size and water behaviour can matter for a path material, but choice needs more than one check.
Diagram feature, job need, match and reason is a model for judging material suitability.
Vocabulary term rock means a solid thing from the ground; example: This is a safe rock sample.
Vocabulary term hard means not easy to mark or change; example: This hard rock takes little mark.
Vocabulary term slate means a rock that can split into thin sheets; example: A slate tile can cover a roof.
Vocabulary term property means a thing you can check; example: This slate is thin.
Retrieval question from SoW C41: What two checks did we use on rocks? Answer: Mark and water-through tests.
Retrieval question from SoW C40: Name one way to sort rocks. Answer: By what they look or feel like.
Retrieval question from SoW C35: What helps bones move? Answer: Muscles.
The “Slate roof” picture shows thin slate tiles used for roof coverings where suitable.
The “Chalk mark” picture is a model; check a real sample's marking property rather than assuming every rock marks alike.
New transfer hinge and parallel: A new sample stays firm in a safe pressure test. Which possible job fits that clue? Correct: A path stone if it stays firm.
